beneficiaryAdministration:
Programme Scope

This Programme supports the contracting of External Service Providers to help beneficiaries design/upscale/commercialise space-enabled green solutions or adopt commercially available ones, contributing to the transition towards more sustainable and circular business innovation practices, processes, and partnerships.

This Open Call targets applicants who are interested in using downstream space data to create solutions that have a positive environmental impact, either: for the company itself (e.g., by improving current processes to minimize resources, waste, pollution, etc.) – Type A Transformation Project or for its users (e.g., by creating new or improving existing products for better resource management, environmental monitoring, etc.) – Type B Transformation Project

Applicants should demonstrate their potential to leverage downstream space data, such as Earth Observation (EO), remote sensing, satellite navigation, etc. The program places a particular focus on supporting solutions in areas such as:

  1. Improvement of circularity in terms of improved use of resources and waste management
  2. Safe, resource-efficient, and environmentally friendly management of primary, secondary, and critical raw materials
  3. Improved environmental monitoring

Max. Grant Amount

Each selected beneficiary can receive up to 50,000 EUR to implement its project, based on the budget information indicated in the application form and paid out after successful completion and verification of results.

How to apply

Applications must be submitted via our online portal https://opportunities.getonepass.eu/opportunities/financial-support-program/2nd-open-call within the indicated deadline.

Who can apply

Single entities applying as: Self-employed individuals, Micro Enterprises, Small Enterprises, Medium-sized Enterprises, including start-ups and scale-ups.

At the time of application, these single entities should be legally registered in any EU Member State and its Overseas Countries and Territories (OCT) or Horizon Europe Associated Countries.

Number of grants available

We aim to support approximately 22 Projects in this Open Call. In particular, we aim to support approximately 6 projects requesting a scale-up voucher (i.e. up to 50.000 EUR) and 16 projects requesting an ideation/ commercialization voucher (i.e. up to 25.000 EUR). This number may vary, depending on the different types of projects to be funded and the actual requested budget.

The total budget available for this Open Call is 694 520,00 EUR. The budget may increase during the application period. In such an event, the Guide for Applicants will be updated accordingly.

The final number of awarded projects is determined by the total budget allocated to this Open Call and the overall quality of the selected projects.

Evaluation process

We will evaluate only complete proposals that are submitted via our official application platform within the indicated deadline.

The evaluation process consists of the following steps:

  1. Step 1 will check the proposals against eligibility criteria.
  2. Step 2 (if necessary) will perform a pre-scoring process.
  3. Step 3 will involve experts’ evaluation to assess the proposal according to the criteria.
  4. Step 4 when the Selection Committee will decide the “provisional list of FSTP recipients” during the Consensus Meeting
  5. Step 5 will include the legal screening of the pre-selected entities before they are invited to sign the Sub-Grant Agreement.

● Ideation projects: up to 25,000 EUR

● Scale-Up projects: up to 50,000 EUR

● Commercialisation projects: up to 25,000 EUR

The projects will be implemented with the support of External Service Providers and 100% of the financial support will be allocated to them (no extra costs are reimbursed). The eligible services and a list of External Service Providers (not exhaustive) can be found in the Guide for Applicants here: https://2nd-financing.project-fierce.eu/

Each beneficiary can receive as many services as needed, as long as they do not surpass the maximum amount they are allowed to spend on service providers i.e. 50,000 EUR.

Beneficiaries supported under the First Financial Support Program can apply to the FIERCE 2nd Open Call for Financing, as long as they do not exceed the maximum financial support available per beneficiary (50,000 EUR).

Each beneficiary will be assigned a Lead Mentor who will guide and support them through the programme.

lastVerifiedRecord.description: ApplyESA BIC Andalusia2026-09-28T14:53:44+02:00 The Open Call for Proposals is now OPENNext cut-off date: 30 October 2026 at 12:00 CET. Download the Application Package below to apply to ESA BIC Andalusia Download the Application Package (.zip)Who Can ApplyEnsure your startup can join our incubation programme To be eligible for ESA BIC Andalusia, your startup or business idea must meet the following criteria: Space-Related InnovationYour business must have a solid connection to space-related technology, expertise, or applications. This connection can be categorized as either Downstream or Upstream: Downstream This involves the application or exploitation of space systems or technologies in non-space domains. Your business idea may focus on: Applications utilizing satellite navigation, earth observation, or satellite communication.Technology transfer involving space-related hardware, software, or intellectual property.Providing solutions that leverage space data or technology to innovate in other sectorsUpstream This relates to the development of new technologies intended for use within the space sector. Examples include: Developing new systems, subsystems, or components for space missions.Technologies and services designed for use on space missions or in human spaceflight activities.Your application must clearly justify the space connection, demonstrating how it advances or innovates within the space sector. It is crucial that the space connection is clear and justified in your application. For further guidance on ensuring your idea meets the necessary criteria, please consult the Space Connection Assessment document. This will help you evaluate and articulate the space connection of your business idea to meet the requirements set by ESA BIC Andalusia. Viable Business PlanYou must present a clear and viable business plan outlining your strategy for growth, the market potential of your product or service, and how your space-related innovation will be commercialized. The business plan should also detail financial projections, key milestones, and risk management strategies. Company AgeNew or existing companies less than 5 years old. If Your Company is Already Established Your startup must be legally registered in Spain and must not be older than five years at the time of application. If Your Company is Not Yet Established You are eligible to apply as an informal group of entrepreneurs, provided you commit to legally registering your startup in Andalusia upon acceptance into the programme. Company LocationYour business must be, or commit to being, located in Andalusia during the incubation period. ESA BIC Andalusia is strategically located in the Naves de Renfe building in the San Jerónimo district of Seville, near the Spanish Space Agency headquarters. Commitment to the programmeYour team must be fully committed to engaging with the ESA BIC Andalusia programme throughout the entire incubation period. This includes regular attendance at workshops, mentoring sessions, and events organized by the incubator, as well as making full use of the resources provided. How to ApplyFollow these steps and turn your ideas into successful businesses Check Your EligibilityEnsure your startup meets the eligibility criteria for ESA BIC Andalusia. If you are unsure, visit the Who can apply section for more information. Contact Our TeamIt is highly recommended to contact ESA BIC Andalusia in advance to inform us about your intention to apply. The team will assist you in determining whether your business idea is suitable for incubation and will explain what is needed from the applicant. Download The Application FormsThe Open Call for Proposals is OPEN. All application forms and supporting documents are available below. Download the full Application Package and submit your proposal. Download the Application Package (.zip)Prepare Your ApplicationBefore you begin filling out any forms, it is strongly recommended that you carefully read all the provided documents. Application Templates The Application Package contains the following documents: ESA BIC Andalusia Open Call (call conditions and process) ESA BIC Application Form (the document to complete and submit, including its annexes) Draft Incubation Contract Space Connection Assessment Supporting Documents Make sure to thoroughly review all supporting documents, particularly the Draft Incubation Contract. This document is crucial for understanding your contractual obligations and ensuring you are fully informed before proceeding with your application. Documents Preparation Application Form: complete all required sections following the instructions inside the form. It replaces the previous separate templates (cover letter, business plan and incubation proposal). Include details on how you intend to use the incentive funding. The form must be signed by the majority shareholder, or by shareholders jointly holding more than 50% of the shares; the signature also confirms acceptance of the Incubation Contract conditions. Draft Incubation Contract: read it carefully before applying. Modifications or amendments may only be considered in exceptional cases. Space Connection Assessment: use this document to evaluate and articulate the space connection of your business idea. Application SubmissionBefore submitting, review all your documents carefully. Ensure that each section is completed according to the instructions provided in the templates. Once everything is in order, submit the completed Application Form as a single PDF file to opencall-esabic-andalusia@catec.aero, with the subject ‘ESA BIC Andalusia Open Call’. Important: Ensure your submission is completed before the announced cut-off date. Submissions received after the cut-off deadline will not be considered for that particular round. Evaluation ProcessAfter submitting your application to ESA BIC Andalusia, the post-submission process is as follows: TOB Review: Your application first undergoes an initial screening by the Tender Opening Board (TOB). The TOB checks the completeness of your application and whether it meets the formal requirements. TEB Evaluation: If the TOB process is successful, your application is then forwarded to the Tender Evaluation Board (TEB). The TEB is composed of representatives from the European Space Agency (ESA), the Spanish Space Agency (AEE), ESA BIC Andalusia, the Junta de Andalucía as regional co-funder, and external experts. This board will conduct a detailed evaluation of your proposal, focusing on technical feasibility, business potential, and alignment with the goals of the ESA BIC programme. Interview with TEB: As part of the TEB evaluation, you will be invited to present your business idea. This interview, conducted in English, is a crucial step, allowing you to discuss your project in detail and answer any questions from the board. Ensure that you carefully prepare for the TEB interview by thoroughly understanding your proposal and being ready to discuss both the technical and business aspects in detail. TEB Decision & Certificate: Once the TEB has completed its evaluation and your interview, you will be formally notified of the outcome. If approved, ESA will issue your official TEB Selection Certificate, confirming your eligibility to secure the Junta de Andalucía’s co-financing approval prior to final contract signature. Detailed instructions for the co-financing application process follow. Contract Signing: Once the contract is signed, your startup officially begins its incubation period with ESA BIC Andalusia. Regional Co-Funding ApplicationAfter receiving your TEB Selection Certificate, you must submit your regional co-funding application via the Junta de Andalucía’s e-Office portal before the deadline indicated in the Call to secure co-funding from the regional authority. Complete the non-competitive grant form as established in the Open Call documentation and the referenced Regulatory Bases, attach your TEB Selection Certificate and all required administrative documents, and submit through the official channel. Regional co-funding is awarded to projects that have passed the TEB evaluation and meet the formal eligibility requirements set out in the Open Call and Regulatory Bases. Applications are processed in order of validation and subject to budget availability. You will then be notified of the award decision. Sign Contract & Start IncubationUpon confirmation of your regional co-funding, you will sign the Incubation Contract. With your signature in place, your incubation officially begins, granting you access to a comprehensive suite of programme services—high-level mentoring, state-of-the-art technical facilities, expert business coaching, dedicated legal & IPR support, the 60K € financing package, dynamic networking events, and community collaboration opportunities. Welcome aboard: incubation officially starts! Open Call for ProposalsESA BIC Andalusia operates under a continuous Open Call system, meaning that applications are accepted year-round. Proposals are evaluated at specific cut-off dates. The Open Call is now OPEN. Next cut-off date: 30 October 2026 at 12:00 CET. Download the Application Package above and submit your proposal to participate in the next evaluation round. Need Assistance?If you have any questions or require further clarification, please contact the ESA BIC Andalusia team directly. You are also encouraged to consult the FAQ for additional guidance and information. Contact the ESA BIC Andalusia teamConsult the Frequently Asked Questions

record.description: ApplyESA BIC Andalusia2026-10-29T15:23:31+01:00 Who Can ApplyEnsure your startup can join our incubation programme To be eligible for ESA BIC Andalusia, your startup or business idea must meet the following criteria: Space-Related InnovationYour business must have a solid connection to space-related technology, expertise, or applications. This connection can be categorized as either Downstream or Upstream: Downstream This involves the application or exploitation of space systems or technologies in non-space domains. Your business idea may focus on: Applications utilizing satellite navigation, earth observation, or satellite communication.Technology transfer involving space-related hardware, software, or intellectual property.Providing solutions that leverage space data or technology to innovate in other sectorsUpstream This relates to the development of new technologies intended for use within the space sector. Examples include: Developing new systems, subsystems, or components for space missions.Technologies and services designed for use on space missions or in human spaceflight activities.Your application must clearly justify the space connection, demonstrating how it advances or innovates within the space sector. It is crucial that the space connection is clear and justified in your application. For further guidance on ensuring your idea meets the necessary criteria, please consult the Space Connection Assessment document. This will help you evaluate and articulate the space connection of your business idea to meet the requirements set by ESA BIC Andalusia. Viable Business PlanYou must present a clear and viable business plan outlining your strategy for growth, the market potential of your product or service, and how your space-related innovation will be commercialized. The business plan should also detail financial projections, key milestones, and risk management strategies. Company AgeNew or existing companies less than 5 years old. If Your Company is Already Established Your startup must be legally registered in Spain and must not be older than five years at the time of application. If Your Company is Not Yet Established You are eligible to apply as an informal group of entrepreneurs, provided you commit to legally registering your startup in Andalusia upon acceptance into the programme. Company LocationYour business must be, or commit to being, located in Andalusia during the incubation period. ESA BIC Andalusia is strategically located in the Naves de Renfe building in the San Jerónimo district of Seville, near the Spanish Space Agency headquarters. Commitment to the programmeYour team must be fully committed to engaging with the ESA BIC Andalusia programme throughout the entire incubation period. This includes regular attendance at workshops, mentoring sessions, and events organized by the incubator, as well as making full use of the resources provided. How to ApplyFollow these steps and turn your ideas into successful businesses Check Your EligibilityEnsure your startup meets the eligibility criteria for ESA BIC Andalusia. If you are unsure, visit the Who can apply section for more information. Contact Our TeamIt is highly recommended to contact ESA BIC Andalusia in advance to inform us about your intention to apply. The team will assist you in determining whether your business idea is suitable for incubation and will explain what is needed from the applicant. Download The Application FormsAll application forms and supporting documents are available below. Download the full Application Package and submit your proposal. Download the Application Package (.zip)Prepare Your ApplicationBefore you begin filling out any forms, it is strongly recommended that you carefully read all the provided documents. Application Templates The Application Package contains the following documents: ESA BIC Andalusia Open Call (call conditions and process) ESA BIC Application Form (the document to complete and submit, including its annexes) Draft Incubation Contract Space Connection Assessment Supporting Documents Make sure to thoroughly review all supporting documents, particularly the Draft Incubation Contract. This document is crucial for understanding your contractual obligations and ensuring you are fully informed before proceeding with your application. Documents Preparation Application Form: complete all required sections following the instructions inside the form. It replaces the previous separate templates (cover letter, business plan and incubation proposal). Include details on how you intend to use the incentive funding. The form must be signed by the majority shareholder, or by shareholders jointly holding more than 50% of the shares; the signature also confirms acceptance of the Incubation Contract conditions. Draft Incubation Contract: read it carefully before applying. Modifications or amendments may only be considered in exceptional cases. Space Connection Assessment: use this document to evaluate and articulate the space connection of your business idea. Application SubmissionBefore submitting, review all your documents carefully. Ensure that each section is completed according to the instructions provided in the templates. Once everything is in order, submit the completed Application Form as a single PDF file to opencall-esabic-andalusia@catec.aero, with the subject ‘ESA BIC Andalusia Open Call’. Important: Ensure your submission is completed before the announced cut-off date. Submissions received after the cut-off deadline will not be considered for that particular round. Evaluation ProcessAfter submitting your application to ESA BIC Andalusia, the post-submission process is as follows: TOB Review: Your application first undergoes an initial screening by the Tender Opening Board (TOB). The TOB checks the completeness of your application and whether it meets the formal requirements. TEB Evaluation: If the TOB process is successful, your application is then forwarded to the Tender Evaluation Board (TEB). The TEB is composed of representatives from the European Space Agency (ESA), the Spanish Space Agency (AEE), ESA BIC Andalusia, the Junta de Andalucía as regional co-funder, and external experts. This board will conduct a detailed evaluation of your proposal, focusing on technical feasibility, business potential, and alignment with the goals of the ESA BIC programme. Interview with TEB: As part of the TEB evaluation, you will be invited to present your business idea. This interview, conducted in English, is a crucial step, allowing you to discuss your project in detail and answer any questions from the board. Ensure that you carefully prepare for the TEB interview by thoroughly understanding your proposal and being ready to discuss both the technical and business aspects in detail. TEB Decision & Certificate: Once the TEB has completed its evaluation and your interview, you will be formally notified of the outcome. If approved, ESA will issue your official TEB Selection Certificate, confirming your eligibility to secure the Junta de Andalucía’s co-financing approval prior to final contract signature. Detailed instructions for the co-financing application process follow. Contract Signing: Once the contract is signed, your startup officially begins its incubation period with ESA BIC Andalusia. Regional Co-Funding ApplicationAfter receiving your TEB Selection Certificate, you must submit your regional co-funding application via the Junta de Andalucía’s e-Office portal before the deadline indicated in the Call to secure co-funding from the regional authority. Complete the non-competitive grant form as established in the Open Call documentation and the referenced Regulatory Bases, attach your TEB Selection Certificate and all required administrative documents, and submit through the official channel. Regional co-funding is awarded to projects that have passed the TEB evaluation and meet the formal eligibility requirements set out in the Open Call and Regulatory Bases. Applications are processed in order of validation and subject to budget availability. You will then be notified of the award decision. Sign Contract & Start IncubationUpon confirmation of your regional co-funding, you will sign the Incubation Contract. With your signature in place, your incubation officially begins, granting you access to a comprehensive suite of programme services—high-level mentoring, state-of-the-art technical facilities, expert business coaching, dedicated legal & IPR support, the 60K € financing package, dynamic networking events, and community collaboration opportunities. Welcome aboard: incubation officially starts! Open Call for ProposalsESA BIC Andalusia operates under a continuous Open Call system, meaning that applications are accepted year-round. Proposals are evaluated at specific cut-off dates. Submissions are now closed Download the Application Package above and prepare your proposal to participate in the next evaluation round. Need Assistance?If you have any questions or require further clarification, please contact the ESA BIC Andalusia team directly. You are also encouraged to consult the FAQ for additional guidance and information. Contact the ESA BIC Andalusia teamConsult the Frequently Asked Questions

This document is crucial for understanding your contractual obligations and ensuring you are fully informed before proceeding with your application. Documents Preparation Application Form: complete all required sections following the instructions inside the form. It replaces the previous separate templates (cover letter, business plan and incubation proposal). Include details on how you intend to use the incentive funding. The form must be signed by the majority shareholder, or by shareholders jointly holding more than 50% of the shares; the signature also confirms acceptance of the Incubation Contract conditions. Draft Incubation Contract: read it carefully before applying. Modifications or amendments may only be considered in exceptional cases. Space Connection Assessment: use this document to evaluate and articulate the space connection of your business idea. Application SubmissionBefore submitting, review all your documents carefully. Ensure that each section is completed according to the instructions provided in the templates. Once everything is in order, submit the completed Application Form as a single PDF file to opencall-esabic-andalusia@catec.aero, with the subject ‘ESA BIC Andalusia Open Call’. The TOB checks the completeness of your application and whether it meets the formal requirements. TEB Evaluation: If the TOB process is successful, your application is then forwarded to the Tender Evaluation Board (TEB). The TEB is composed of representatives from the European Space Agency (ESA), the Spanish Space Agency (AEE), ESA BIC Andalusia, the Junta de Andalucía as regional co-funder, and external experts. This board will conduct a detailed evaluation of your proposal, focusing on technical feasibility, business potential, and alignment with the goals of the ESA BIC programme. This interview, conducted in English, is a crucial step, allowing you to discuss your project in detail and answer any questions from the board. Ensure that you carefully prepare for the TEB interview by thoroughly understanding your proposal and being ready to discuss both the technical and business aspects in detail. record.eligibilityText: ASAP & Digitaler Zwilling Österreich 2026 Die Ausschreibung 2026 im Thema Weltraum & Digitalisierung Das Österreichische Weltraumprogramm ASAP und die Initiative Digitaler Zwilling Österreich bieten mit der Ausschreibung 2026 breite Möglichkeiten für Projekte in den Themen Erdbeobachtung, Navigation und Telekommunikation, Technologien für die Raumfahrt sowie Weltraumwissenschaften und Exploration. Insgesamt steht ein Budget von ca. 13 Mio. EUR zur Verfügung. Jetzt einreichen Hinweis: Bitte lesen Sie vor der Einreichung alle Informationen auf dieser Seite aufmerksam durch. Was wird gefördert? Im Fokus der Förderung stehen F&E-Projekte an der Schnittstelle zwischen Weltraum und Digitalen Technologien, zur Anwendung von Satellitendaten, Produktentwicklung für die Raumfahrt mit Hebelwirkung in die ESA, EU und globale institutionelle und kommerzielle Märkte sowie die Beteiligungen an Weltraummissionen. Wer wird gefördert? Antragsberechtigt sind Universitäten, Forschungseinrichtungen, KMU, Industrieunternehmen, Bedarfsträger und sonstige Organisationen. Wie hoch ist die Förderung? Die Förderhöhe richtet sich nach dem eingereichten Förderinstrument und der Organisationsart zwischen 35-100% der Projektkosten. Was sind die Einreichkriterien? Siehe Ausschreibungs- und Instrumentenleitfäden Wie erfolgt die Einreichung? Die Einreichung erfolgt über das eCall-System der FFG, in dem der Projektinhalt und die –kosten dargestellt werden. Welche Dokumente für die Einreichung erforderlich sein werden, wird im Ausschreibungsleitfaden angeführt. Wann gibt es eine Entscheidung? Die Förderentscheidung ist für April 2027 geplant.
